Title: Seaguar Tatsu Fluorocarbon
Description:
Seaguar Tatsu Fluorocarbon

Diameter chart, reel capacity & backing guide

Tatsu is Seaguar's double-structure fluorocarbon main line. Two fluorocarbon resins are combined in one line, with Seaguar emphasizing suppleness and strength. This guide covers the listed 4-25 lb sizes and helps you budget a full fill or a working section over backing.

Construction
Double-structure 100% fluorocarbon
Listed strengths
4-25 lb
Line type
Fluorocarbon main line

Is Tatsu right for your setup?

Consider Tatsu when you want to cast fluorocarbon directly, especially when handling and the amount of premium line used matter to your setup. A partial fill over sound mono backing can reduce how much Tatsu is tied up below the working line. It does not remove the need to choose a manageable diameter: thick fluorocarbon can be awkward on a compact spinning spool even if the capacity number is acceptable.

Choosing your setup

Choosing your Tatsu strength

Start with the lighter 4-8 lb options when considering a light spinning setup, then check your rod, cover, and drag setting. Tatsu's 4 lb and 6 lb entries are not interchangeable in a capacity calculation: their listed inch diameters are .006 and .008.

For baitcasting setups, compare the 10-15 lb choices with the demands of your lure and cover before moving into 17-25 lb. The heavier sizes are not simply better versions of the lighter line. Their extra spool volume can shorten the useful working length.

Tatsu 20 lb and 22 lb both round to .015 inch in the manufacturer chart, although their millimeter entries differ. ReelCalc's inch-based calculation will therefore give them the same capacity. That is a limit of the rounded inputs, not proof that the lines are physically identical.

This is a specification-based setup guide, not a hands-on Tatsu performance test.

Backing, working line & leaders

Decide how much Tatsu you need

For a full Tatsu spool, use the full-capacity result. For a shorter working section, allow for casts, fish runs, damaged-line removal, and repeated retying before assigning the remaining space to backing.

Keep backing below the working line

Mono backing sits underneath the Tatsu. Choose a working length that keeps its connection below the line you normally fish, and do not reuse backing that is damaged or slipping on the arbor.

Match the retail package

The 200-yard package is listed throughout this range. The 1,000-yard package is not listed for every strength: the current chart excludes 4 lb and 25 lb. Check your selected row before assuming a bulk spool exists.

Tatsu questions, answered

Is Tatsu a main line or leader material?

Seaguar sells Tatsu as fluorocarbon main line. You can use a short piece as a leader, but that does not make Tatsu the material filling a braid spool. Calculate capacity using the actual main line.

Does Tatsu have the same diameter as InvizX?

Not at every strength. For example, the current 20 lb entries are .015 inch for Tatsu and .016 inch for InvizX. Use exact product-and-strength diameters instead of treating all Seaguar fluorocarbon as one line.

Will one 200-yard Tatsu spool fill my reel?

Select your reel and Tatsu strength to check. A result below 200 yards means one full retail spool should cover that calculated fill; a higher result calls for more main line or an intentional backing plan. Stop at the reel's recommended fill level.

Title: Seaguar AbrazX Fluorocarbon
Description:
Seaguar AbrazX Fluorocarbon

Diameter chart, reel capacity & backing guide

AbrazX is Seaguar's abrasion-focused fluorocarbon main line. The manufacturer positions it for fishing around cover such as rocks, docks, and timber. Its 4-25 lb range includes very different diameters, so select a strength before checking reel capacity or buying a spool.

Construction
100% fluorocarbon
Listed strengths
4-25 lb
Line type
Fluorocarbon main line

Is AbrazX right for your setup?

AbrazX is a candidate for presentations where line contacts cover and you want fluorocarbon as the working main line. Its abrasion-focused positioning is not permission to ignore nicks or tighten the drag excessively. Check the line after contact with rough cover and retie when needed; allow spare working length for that maintenance when planning backing.

Choosing your setup

Choosing your AbrazX strength

A light spinning setup and a heavier cover-oriented baitcaster should not receive the same AbrazX just because both reels list a 10 lb capacity. Use the rod, lure, cover, and fish to choose strength; the reel label is a capacity reference, not a required line choice.

The 10, 12, and 15 lb entries step from .010 to .011 to .013 inch. Moving from 15 lb to 17 lb increases the listed diameter again, to .015 inch. Check the capacity change instead of assuming each two-pound increase takes the same amount of space.

The 20-25 lb sizes occupy substantially more space than the lighter options and can be difficult to manage on small spinning reels. More abrasion-focused material does not make every diameter suitable for every reel.

Backing, working line & leaders

Allow for retying

Fishing close to abrasive cover can consume working line as worn sections are removed. Do not use a backing plan that leaves only enough AbrazX for one maximum cast with no reserve.

A full fill or a top section

A full AbrazX fill avoids a backing connection. A shorter working section over mono can save line on a deep spool. The calculator checks space for either plan; neither result is a guarantee of knot strength or abrasion resistance.

Inspect the contact section

Check the line nearest the lure after rough contact. Replace nicked or weakened sections rather than relying on the product's abrasion-resistant positioning. Recheck the remaining working length as it gets shorter.

AbrazX questions, answered

Is AbrazX the same line as InvizX?

No. They are separate fluorocarbon products with different manufacturer positioning. Even where their published diameter entries match, a capacity match is not evidence of identical handling or abrasion performance.

Can AbrazX fill a spinning reel?

It is main-line fluorocarbon, but choose a diameter that your spinning setup can manage. Thick line may fit by volume while still springing off a small spool. Capacity and handling are separate checks.

Does the 4 lb AbrazX come in a bulk spool?

The current manufacturer chart and assigned variants list a 200-yard spool for 4 lb. The 1,000-yard option starts at 6 lb in the specifications used here; retail stock can change.

Seaguar Red Label Fluorocarbon

Red Label is Seaguar's value-oriented fluorocarbon main line, with manufacturer positioning aimed at baitcasting reels. The current range runs from 4 to 20 lb. Package length changes at the heavy end, so a Red Label spool is not automatically a 200-yard spool.

Is Red Label right for your setup?

Consider Red Label for a fluorocarbon main-line setup when cost and regular respooling are part of the decision. Match its diameter to the baitcaster, rod, and presentation before deciding on a full fill. If you are looking for a light spinning line, do not assume every fluorocarbon marketed for baitcasting will handle the same way as a softer main line.

Choosing your setup

Choosing your Red Label strength

Use the exact Red Label entry rather than borrowing an InvizX or Tatsu diameter. Red Label 12 lb is listed at .012 inch, compared with .011 inch for both of those other models; it occupies more spool space in the inch-based calculation.

The 10-15 lb options give several intermediate choices for baitcasting applications, but the correct choice still depends on lure, cover, and your rod. Moving to 17 or 20 lb reduces capacity and is not an automatic improvement for open-water fishing.

For a partial fill, leave enough working Red Label to absorb retying and damaged-line removal. The backing knot should remain below the line used during normal casts and fish runs, not arrive at the lure after a few trips.

Backing, working line & leaders

Check yards, not just pound test

The assigned retail variant for 20 lb is 175 yards, while the lighter retail entries are 200 yards. Both the strength and the package length matter when checking whether one spool covers your plan.

Bulk line still needs a fill limit

A 1,000-yard package can cover multiple fills, but it does not change your reel's capacity. Use the calculation as a starting point and stop at the reel manufacturer's fill level.

Main line and leader are different roles

A short Red Label leader on braid does not use a full spool of Red Label. For that arrangement, select the braid as the main line in the Wizard and consider the leader separately.

Red Label questions, answered

Is Red Label a fluorocarbon-coated nylon line?

No. Seaguar identifies this product as 100% fluorocarbon main line, not fluorocarbon-coated nylon.

Why does 20 lb show 175 yards?

That is the assigned retail package on Seaguar's current product listing and chart. Unassigned 200-yard selector combinations are not treated as verified retail packages. A 1,000-yard option is also listed.

Why is the 6 lb diameter different from my other Seaguar line?

Seaguar's Red Label chart and selector list 6 lb at .007 inch and .185 mm. Equal pound-test labels do not require equal diameters across products. Check the package if your line is from a different generation or market.

Choosing your Smackdown strength

Backing, working line & leaders

Plan a useful braid length

Choose a working length that covers casting, runs, and retying. A 150-yard package may be sufficient for that working section even when your reel's full braid capacity is much larger.

Prevent arbor slip

Use a secure attachment appropriate to your reel. Mono backing can provide an anchor and occupy unused spool space; follow the reel manufacturer's braid-attachment guidance and do not confuse backing with a short leader.

Choose the leader separately

A mono or fluorocarbon leader is the section nearest the lure. Choose it for the presentation and cover rather than automatically matching the braid's pound test. Its short length does not determine the reel's full braid capacity.

Smackdown questions, answered

Is Smackdown fluorocarbon?

No. This is eight-strand braided main line. A fluorocarbon leader may be added at the lure end, but that does not change the braid into fluorocarbon.

Why not calculate from the mono-equivalent label?

Mono equivalence is not a universal diameter standard. ReelCalc uses the numeric diameter of the selected product rather than substituting a generic mono pound test for it.

Are these capacities for Flash Green too?

This page's verified source is the current Stealth Gray listing. Check the numeric diameter on the exact Flash Green package before applying the same capacity, especially for older stock or a different market.

Use the length for your strength

Full mono fill

Reusing a backing layer

Only reuse backing that is sound, secure, and long enough to support the intended working line. An estimated backing length cannot reveal the condition of line already hidden under a spool.

A 100-meter package is not 150 yards

Will one package fill a 3000-size reel?
